title: Stars trails over La Silla
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars draw long trails across the sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory, while the trail of an aircraft runs over the horizon. The picture combines a series of night exposures taken looking toward the east.

The trails do not mean the stars are moving. They record the sky's apparent motion over the course of a night, which is really Earth spinning on its axis and carrying the camera with it. The celestial south pole lies out of frame, toward the upper right, and the celestial equator runs from the top left corner of the frame down to the horizon.

Several of the observatory's telescopes appear. Front and centre stands the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, and the NTT and the ESO 3.6-metre telescope stand in the background. Off to the right in the distance is SEST, the Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope.

understand.summary: This is a stack of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla. The individual exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points. Only by combining many exposures can a camera record the sky's slow turning as continuous trails.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: Near the celestial pole, star trails bend into tight circles, while near the celestial equator they run as almost straight lines. That is why the curvature of the trails changes across a wide view like this one.
alt: Star trails arcing over several telescope domes at La Silla, with an aircraft trail over the horizon.
